title: A simple root of a polynomial over a local ring is unique among the lifts congruent to it modulo the maximal ideal
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on Henselian local rings
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma is about a local ring (R, m, kappa) and states that two roots a and b of a polynomial f in R[T] which are congruent modulo m and at which f' is not in m must be equal (statement lines 42310-42316). The proof expands f at a to write the vanishing difference of values as f'(a)(b-a) plus a multiple of (b-a)^2, inverts the derivative, and concludes because b-a lies in the maximal ideal so that 1 + f'(a)^{-1}c(b-a) is a unit (proof lines 42318-42325). The step that carries the content is the Taylor expansion, which the author states and leaves to the reader as routine; everything after it is the standard unit argument in a local ring. H2.
